unmapped_findings: The various heat treatments of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal specimens result in different states of short-range order: maximum ordering after the 250 °C/14 day anneal, minimum ordering after quenching from 1100 or 600 °C, and intermediate degrees of order for the other treatments in Fig. 1 — hence the 300 °C/3 day anneal corresponds to an intermediate degree of order (b0050).
The hardness of the 300 °C/3 d-annealed Fe-16%Al monocrystal equals that of the as-grown monocrystal; it is concluded that short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness (b0050).
Only heat treatments at temperatures above 600 °C affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys significantly (b0051, b0067).

Excess vacancies (introduced by quenching, not by the 300 °C anneal itself) heal out only slowly; the annealing at 300 °C of the Fe-Al alloys even for 14 days may not have been sufficient for the complete elimination of the excess vacancies (b0055).
